Summary: We live as if our choices are real and we are responsible for them - and we hold others responsible too. Strict materialism struggles to ground genuine choice: if every thought is fixed by physics, deliberation is an illusion. Christianity grounds freedom in persons made in God's image, capable of real agency and real responsibility.
KeyPoints: Moral responsibility assumes real choice; Determinism makes deliberation illusory; Persons made in God's image can truly choose
RelatedTopics: Free Will; Moral Responsibility; Image of God
